0.long_answer: The medications that target extracellular serotonin levels primarily do so by inhibiting serotonin reuptake. In addition to SNRIs, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are used to achieve this effect. SSRIs block the reabsorption of serotonin into neurons, thereby increasing its availability in the synaptic cleft, which helps alleviate symptoms of hypochondriasis and other related disorders. Some common examples of SSRIs include fluoxetine, paroxetine, and sertraline.
